Sedona and Grand Canyon Combo, Two Days

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Sedona and Grand Canyon tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for your group across 2 days: the red rocks on one, the South Rim on the other. The row publishes the trip as 2 Days. Multi-day is a written quote until it is priced. A single published day starts from $125 an hour. Below: how the 2 days split, which vehicle fits, and how the quote is built. Call (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 24, 2026

What is a private Sedona and Grand Canyon tour from Phoenix?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for your group across 2 days — red rocks on one, the South Rim on the other — never a seat on a shared coach. 6 vehicles are offered, from 6 to 29 seats. The booking itself is a written quote. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport around both destinations, never entry to either. Your group decides who is aboard and how the hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, waits and drives home. It suits the parties a fixed schedule serves badly. The fare is for the vehicle, never per person. Multi-day is a written quote: the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter and the 29-seat Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) are both on the card, and neither is priced here as an hourly block.

How are the 2 days split between the red rocks and the South Rim?

The tour publishes 2 steps, one for each day, and states the trip as 2 Days. Both hang off the same two fixed points: the stops your group confirms, and the room it has booked for itself between them. Everything else in the window is yours to spend. The site already publishes what the Sedona half looks like alone: "A one-way or round-trip ride north is booked on the Phoenix and Scottsdale to Sedona transfer page; a full day with the vehicle waiting at each trailhead, gallery and tasting room is the Sedona red rocks day trip." Neither step is a timetable: an hourly charter buys time rather than mileage, so a stop written down beforehand costs nothing extra. Day 1: Drive to confirmed Sedona stops; coordinate any trailhead, chapel, or wine-country check-in around current access; overnight at lodging booked directly by the group Day 2: Drive from confirmed lodging to the South Rim entrance and viewpoints allowed by current access and parking; return to Scottsdale

Why book both as one trip instead of 2 separate day tours?

Because of the free-hour ladder, and the difference is arithmetic rather than opinion. The published one-day products request 12 hours for Sedona and 14 for the rim — 26 between them — while this row requests 24 for the pair. Booked separately, each day is its own published day tour. Booked together, the 2 days is one reservation and the price is a written quote. The other half is not money, and the tour answers it in its own words: "A two-day sequence can reduce backtracking compared with separate Scottsdale departures, but the actual route and drive time depend on lodging, park access, stops, traffic, weather, and road conditions."

What does the trip cost, and what is not in it?

The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $145 an hour on a single published day, the hourly rate the checkout uses for that vehicle. Across 2 days the booking is a written quote for the whole vehicle, confirmed in writing before any card is charged, with 8% tax and a 50% deposit on the quote. Three rules build every number: the trip is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, a larger request earns free hours on the ladder, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is charged by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is what the trip is built around. Park entry and day-use parking are set by the agencies that run these places, and no transportation quote covers them. Meals happen at the stops — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." Request a current quote for your dates.

What is worth the red rock day?

The Sedona half is a viewpoint-and-trailhead day, and the 4 public landmarks the area guide names fill it: Cathedral Rock, Bell Rock, Chapel of the Holy Cross and Red Rock State Park. The vehicle waits at each one, which is what a rental cannot do. As the area guide puts it: "The Village of Oak Creek features Bell Rock views and access to popular trails." Which the group walks is decided on the morning, not on the form. The distance question is answered by that page, not by us: it states Sedona as 115 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor. A group that wants the red rocks alone books the Sedona red rocks day trip; the tasting rooms, the Verde Valley wine tour.

What happens on the South Rim day?

The rim half is the longer of the 2, and the 4 landmarks its area guide publishes are what a group reaches: Mather Point, Bright Angel Trail, South Kaibab Trail and Desert View Watchtower. The vehicle waits while you are out. The guide's description of the first stop: "Mather Point offers the classic first view, while the Rim Trail connects overlooks for miles." Nothing here states a shuttle timetable, a trail condition or an entry rule — the park publishes those, and its official page is cited below. The same page states the distance from Phoenix Sky Harbor to Grand Canyon Village as 230 miles, which is why this half wants a whole day.

Is one long day enough, or is 2 days the better trip?

The destination page answers that, and this 2-day trip is what it answers with: "Groups either book a single long day or add a night in Tusayan or Flagstaff" What is booked here is the transportation across both days; where the group stays is booked by the group. The rest of that published paragraph makes the case: "This is a long day rather than an afternoon out: the drive each way, plus the time you actually want at the rim." A single rim day is published on its own; this page is for a group that wants the red rocks too. Where the group sleeps is its own booking, in the tour's own words: "Choose and book a Sedona or Flagstaff hotel directly based on current availability, policies, and budget. Send the confirmed property and check-in time for transportation review." What is sold here is the vehicle, the chauffeur and the hours: "The reservations team confirms the hours before anything is paid"

Where can the trip start, what should we bring, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in Phoenix or Scottsdale — or any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page — not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things: the dates, the headcount and one address. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address and one phone we call keeps a group together; anyone flying in early is a transfer of its own. Bags have a published cap per vehicle rather than a house rule: the Maybach Jet Sprinter takes 4, the Executive Black Sprinter 40, and the Mini Bus (24 Pax) carries no owner-confirmed number, so its fit is confirmed in writing. The chauffeur is a resource: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Anything the form cannot price goes to the desk on (623) 986-6339.
